react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on galactose metabolism as the dominant affected system in this metabolomics comparison. RaMP multi-database ORA returned Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043, KEGG:map00052) at the top rank with FDR = 2.83e-11 and a fold-enrichment of ~1400×, driven by four input metabolites: galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, and glycerol. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirmed the same KEGG:hsa00052 with p = 3.25e-07, hitting the identical four compounds. Mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis independently recovered Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism, p = 0.008) with near-complete pathway overlap (10 of 11 compounds), further validating the signal through mass-based evidence. The four driver metabolites form a structurally coherent input set: galactinol is the direct galactosyl donor to myo-inositol (forming the galactinol-raffinose series), sucrose feeds the Leloir pathway, and glycerol is the terminal triose from galactose catabolism. The treatment therefore appears to perturb the Leloir pathway and downstream sugar-alcohol metabolism, consistent with altered galactose clearance or flux through the galactose-glucose interconversion arm. A secondary consensus on glycerophospholipid biosynthesis (WP:WP2533 / MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism) was independently reached by RaMP (FDR = 1.74e-04) and Mummichog (p = 0.011), anchored by myo-inositol and glycerol. Dopamine and 8(S)-HPETE each appeared in single tools but did not achieve cross-paradigm consensus and are not classified as driver metabolites here.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis tools converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in the treatment group. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) and Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043; KEGG:map00052) both at FDR = 2.83e-11 (rank 0–1). Mummichog m/z-direct activity independently recovered the same pathway as Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism, p = 0.014, rank 4). The four driver metabolites are galactinol (KEGG:C01235), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116), all confirmed members of the hit lists across RaMP and Mummichog with strong fold-enrichment scores. Secondary pathway hits include GPCR downstream signalling (REACT:R-HSA-388396, FDR = 9.38e-06) and Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p = 0.017). 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823) appears only in a single tool without cross-paradigm consensus and is not classified as a driver metabolite.

  "narrative_text": "Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on galactose metabolism as the dominant affected system in this metabolomics comparison. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on galactose metabolism as the dominant affected system in this metabolomics comparison. RaMP multi-database ORA returned Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043, KEGG:map00052) at the top rank with FDR = 2.83e-11 and a fold-enrichment of ~1400×, driven by four input metabolites: galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, and glycerol. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirmed the same KEGG:hsa00052 with p = 3.25e-07, hitting the identical four compounds. Mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis independently recovered Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism, p = 0.008) with near-complete pathway overlap (10 of 11 compounds), further validating the signal through mass-based evidence. The four driver metabolites form a structurally coherent input set: galactinol is the direct galactosyl donor to myo-inositol (forming the galactinol-raffinose series), sucrose feeds the Leloir pathway, and glycerol is the terminal triose from galactose catabolism. The treatment therefore appears to perturb the Leloir pathway and downstream sugar-alcohol metabolism, consistent with altered galactose clearance or flux through the galactose-glucose interconversion arm. A secondary consensus on glycerophospholipid biosynthesis (WP:WP2533 / MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism) was independently reached by RaMP (FDR = 1.74e-04) and Mummichog (p = 0.011), anchored by myo-inositol and glycerol. Dopamine and 8(S)-HPETE each appeared in single tools but did not achieve cross-paradigm consensus and are not classified as driver metabolites here.
